I’ll check the handoff against the current Lean tree, manuscript sources, and package pins. Then I’ll assign separate proof and review packets for the handle reduction and the selected-collar estimates.

The public Gauss and height results replayed at the starting revision. I also found index-rearrangement and handle-attachment theorems in the pinned geometry package. I’m connecting them to the selected height so the auxiliary Morse function retains its actual critical points and indices. On the disk side, the newer companion manuscript gives separate bounds for the joined path and the capped exterior.

The disk proof now turns supplied open comparison-ball charts into disjoint closed disk markings. For \(I<5T/4\), Lean bounds both physical chiral energies on the entire complement of that same marked family. The remaining analytic step is to control the cutoff error on those disks. On the topology side, the marked gluing maps now elaborate on the quotient, and the smooth seam check is underway.

The public build now carries the inclusive \(64\pi^2/9\) bound through to a regular band or an actual two-handle attachment at the selected point. The remaining topology question is how the two end bodies meet that band. I’m checking the end-count bounds separately from the smooth maps needed to identify those bodies.

The companion manuscript gained a construction that bisects four physical measures while preserving the original charged disk inside a larger marked disk. I’m checking what that construction gives Lean in the full range \(I<2T\), including the cost a repair must pay on the disk side. The smooth construction and its measured consequences will be identified separately in the assessment.

Lean now verifies that, given the measured division on the marked disks, both full exterior charges fall below \(T\) throughout \(I<2T\). It also proves that a positive same-type cap below the joined wall requires a definite saving on the disk side. The public build passed, and the rebuilt PDF and web blueprint now include both results.

**Edition 03 now carries the inclusive immersed bound \(E_+\le 64\pi^2/9\) through to an actual smooth middle-band construction.** On the original manifold, Lean produces an ordered Morse function preserving every critical point and index of the selected height. If the middle band is empty, an ambient diffeomorphism transports both its levels and sublevels. If it contains one point, Lean constructs the rounded two-handle there, its full attaching tube, and the regular transports on either side. Recognition still requires identifying the two end bodies and their actual boundary maps.

On the intrinsic route, Lean puts **both physical chiral charges below \(T=4\pi^2\) on the same full exterior** under two distinct hypotheses. The E58 comparison-window construction reaches \(I<5T/4\). Given the newer measured division on nested marked disks, the bound reaches the full range \(I<2T\). With a supplied uniform recognition gap, one division depth forces any qualifying positive same-type cap to save more than that gap on the disk side in **both** chiralities. The repair estimates retain the chosen widths and their derivative costs. Constructing an affordable repair or completing E57 smoothing remains open. No additional smooth type was recognized.

The public `lake build` passed without warnings. All ten package pins matched. Independent checks covered 507 public topic declarations and all 343 declarations referenced by the blueprint, using only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. Both blueprint formats rebuilt. The exact chat source was unavailable for archival.

The public disk theorem now uses both Weyl spectra in the selected metric’s own frame. The signed collar comparison also compiles in both directions, including its equations on protected tubes.
